title: Ireland's Fuel Tax Reversal Exposes the Gap Between Economic Headlines and… · 31 Aug
keywords: Ireland, fuel excise, cost of living, inflation, HICP, energy prices, fiscal policy, Central Bank of Ireland, euro area, household budgets, opposition politics, tax relief, economic outlook
notes: Ireland's government has delayed a planned increase in petrol and diesel excise duties, citing persistent pressure on household budgets as inflation remains stubbornly above the euro-area average. The move has drawn sharp criticism from opposition parties, who argue it represents short-term patchwork rather than a structural fix. The episode lays bare a tension that is reshaping Irish politics and echoing across the European Union: strong macroeconomic data and real household hardship can coexist, and governments are struggling to bridge the gap.
